title: Research Scientist Intern - Neural Representations Compression
description: In the rapidly evolving fields of AI, Augmented Reality (AR), and Virtual Reality (VR), industry compression research is shifting from human-consumed media to non-human-consumed internal neural model states. These representations include latent tensors, weights, Gaussian splats, feature maps, and depth/alpha buffers exchanged between neural networks. As high-capability models exceed on-device compute limits while cloud execution is constrained by latency, privacy, and power, systems are adopting split inference—partitioning model execution between devices and datacenters connected by neural bitstreams. In this architecture, the compression ratio on the split link serves as a primary determinant of round-trip latency, bandwidth efficiency, and battery performance. Advancing compression techniques for neural representations expands beyond rendering outputs to critical non-media data streams. Key emergent areas include Feature Coding for Machines (FCM) for intermediate network features, visual and multimodal token pruning/compression, low-latency action and control streams for embodied systems, KV cache compression for distributed LLM prefill and decode stages, model deltas for on-device personalization, and persistent scene state streams for interactive world models. Establishing specialized compression capabilities across these representations directly impacts the operating efficiency and scalability of split-inference AI and XR applications. The intern will explore several key directions in compression and streaming techniques for neural representations: 1. Latent Vector Compression: Developing efficient quantization, entropy coding, and learned prior models for compact, high-dimensional latent spaces exchanged in split-inference architectures. 2. Gaussian Splat Compression: Creating specialized compression and streaming algorithms that maintain the spatial distribution, opacity, and color parameters of 3D Gaussian splats with high rendering fidelity and low memory footprint. Throughout the project, the intern will conduct a thorough review of existing literature, implement prototype models, and benchmark them against traditional compression methods. The final goal is to develop a neural compression framework that outperforms current techniques in terms of compression ratio, speed, and fidelity. This research not only contributes to the academic field but also has direct applications in improving the operational efficiency of AR/VR systems, ultimately pushing the boundaries of what is possible in digital interaction spaces.

title: Research Scientist Intern - Ads Recommendations
description: Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization. Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Ads Recommendation team within Facebook. This org is directly in charge of recommending ads to users the time they open the app, and thus always gets the first-hand experience of critical pain points to solve. Our interns will have the opportunity to participate in the process of framing practical, high-impact challenges in recommendation into rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance from our research scientists and software engineers. More concretely, while the generative AI innovations in NLP are mainly focusing on optimizing the probabilities of selecting the next word token, in recommendation the vocabulary (contents to suggest) is at a much larger scale and also changing at a fast speed. The preference for these contents can also vary dramatically across users and time. If you’re excited about how to generate the correct sequences of “words” any time the giant number of Facebook users open or scroll down the blue app, come to join us! Our internships are twelve (12) to sixteen (16), or twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

title: Product Yield Enhancement Software Engineer Intern
description: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. As an Intern Product Yield Enhancement (PYE) Software Engineer at Micron Technology, you will help develop software and automation solutions that enable engineers to analyze semiconductor manufacturing and product data more efficiently. PYE engineers work across Research and Development, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, and Global Quality to help take next-generation devices from design to mass production. In this software-focused role, you will work alongside PYE engineers to develop practical tools that turn large and complex engineering datasets into useful information. Projects may include data processing and visualization, engineering workflow automation, web-based tools, AI-assisted engineering applications, and improvements to existing PYE software systems. This internship is intended to provide a hands-on engineering project where you can apply software development skills to real semiconductor manufacturing problems and see the impact of your work. This is a 3-month internship. Responsibilities Your job duties may include: Develop and improve software tools used by PYE engineers for engineering analysis and decision-making. Create automation for processing, analyzing, and visualizing semiconductor manufacturing and product data. Work with large engineering datasets to identify useful patterns, trends, and relationships. Develop scripts, applications, dashboards, reports, or web-based engineering tools. Explore practical applications of AI-assisted engineering and software development. Improve existing engineering workflows through automation and software integration. Debug, test, document, and maintain software used by engineering teams. Collaborate with PYE engineers to understand engineering problems and translate them into effective software solutions. Communicate project results and demonstrate completed tools to engineers and management. During the internship, you'll have an opportunity to: Build software that engineers can use to solve real manufacturing and product problems. Gain experience working with large-scale semiconductor engineering data. Learn how software, data analytics, and semiconductor engineering come together in a high-volume manufacturing environment. Work directly with experienced engineers and software users. Take ownership of a project from problem definition through implementation and demonstration. Explore how modern AI and automation technologies can improve engineering workflows. Minimum Qualifications Pursuing a bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field . Experience programming in at least one language such as Perl, Python, C/C++, Java, or similar . Strong problem-solving and analytical skills. Ability and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies and engineering concepts. Expected graduation date must not be before September 1, 2027 . Preferred Qualifications Experience with Perl . Familiarity with SQL and relational databases . Experience with Linux/Unix environments. Familiarity with web development technologies. Experience working with data visualization or reporting tools. Familiarity with Git or other source-control systems. Exposure to statistics, data science, machine learning, or AI tools. Experience using generative AI and AI-assisted development tools to improve engineering productivity. Semiconductor knowledge is helpful but not required . Ability to work effectively in a diverse, fast-paced engineering environment. Excellent communication skills. Self-motivation, curiosity, and enthusiasm for solving real engineering problems. title: HBM Data Scientist Intern
description: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Department Overview The Data Science team employs advanced analytics, machine learning, and AI technologies to improve semiconductor manufacturing performance and decision-making. By combining statistical methods, engineering expertise, and AI-enabled solutions, the team transforms complex manufacturing data into actionable insights that drive operational excellence and innovation across Micron. Position Overview As a Data Science Intern, you will work at the intersection of statistical analysis, machine learning, and AI agents to solve real-world semiconductor manufacturing challenges. You will apply time-series analytics, change-point detection, machine learning, and large language model (LLM) technologies to identify important patterns in manufacturing data and develop AI-enabled solutions that help engineers make better decisions. Responsibilities Apply statistical and machine learning techniques, including time-series analysis, change-point detection, clustering, and dimensionality reduction, to identify trends and anomalies in semiconductor manufacturing data. Develop and evaluate AI agents and LLM-enabled workflows by integrating analysis tools, designing prompts, and assessing model performance against known outcomes. Extract, clean, integrate, and analyze data using SQL, Python, and analytical tools to support engineering investigations and decision-making. Build reproducible analytics, visualizations, dashboards, and reporting solutions that provide actionable insights to engineering teams. Present technical findings, recommendations, and limitations clearly to engineering partners while supporting continuous improvement initiatives. Minimum Qualifications 0-2 years of relevant experience through coursework, research, internships, academic projects, hackathons, or data science competitions. Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028. Experience with Python for data analysis, including libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, or similar tools, and basic SQL for data extraction and preparation. Knowledge of statistics, machine learning fundamentals, hypothesis testing, regression, clustering, PCA, and data analysis methodologies gained through coursework or projects. Experience using AI technologies, large language models (LLMs), AI agents, or generative AI platforms through academic, personal, or project-based work, along with strong analytical, communication, and collaboration skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with time-series analysis, forecasting, anomaly detection, change-point detection, or statistical modeling techniques. Familiarity with LLM agents, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Model Context Protocol (MCP), LangGraph, prompt engineering, or AI workflow orchestration frameworks. Experience evaluating AI model performance, validating outputs, mitigating hallucinations, or developing AI-assisted applications and workflows. Proficiency with data science and machine learning tools such as Scikit-learn, XGBoost, SHAP, SciPy, R, JMP, Plotly, or similar platforms. Experience applying analytics, machine learning, or AI technologies to manufacturing, engineering, scientific research, or other real-world datasets, with an interest in semiconductor manufacturing and industrial analytics.
